evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database describes 从 in oracle-bone and bronze forms as two 人 figures arranged one after another, the early graph for 從, with the sense ‘follow’. It reports oracle-bone uses for following and for ‘from’, including forms glossed ‘from the west’ and ‘from the east’. The same entry says 人 orientations vary, with most facing left and one recorded facing right; small-seal forms regularize their orientation. These are the database’s analyses and reported examples, not independent inspection of the inscriptions here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 从

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database reports that 從 appears in oracle-bone and bronze material with 彳, and in some bronze forms with 辵, alongside 从. It analyzes 从 as the early form and says the added movement component emphasizes following along a route. However, it separately says the meaning of the 從 form in oracle-bone inscriptions is unclear; it reports bronze uses for accompanying, obeying, and a graph loan for 縱 ‘indulge’. Thus the graph’s history and the attested meanings should not be collapsed into a single chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 从

evidence.source: 中央研究院 (Academia Sinica), 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The entry indexes a 從 oracle-bone example as 合集 29156, bronze examples as 集成 09105 and 10174, and later Chu bamboo-and-silk forms and the 說文 small-seal form. Its account interprets the two 人 as one person ahead and one behind, with ‘follow’ as the original sense; it says 彳 or 辵 is sometimes added to indicate movement. The cited record identifiers document attested graph examples, but do not by themselves date a semantic extension.
evidence.title: 漢字「從」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 金文 / 从 and 從
evidence.text: The database gives the bronze inscription 宰椃角 ‘王各(格)，宰椃从’ as an example of 从 meaning ‘follow’; it also reports a bronze vessel-name use in 任氏从簋 and a personal-name use. For 從 it cites 𨾊弔簋 ‘𨾊弔從王員征楚荊’ for accompanying and 中山王鼎 ‘隹俌(傅)母氏(是)從’ for obeying. These dated inscription records establish distinct contextual uses, but this page does not give absolute dates for each cited item.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 从

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education
evidence.text: The dictionary reports that 說文 treats 从 and 從 as separate entries: 从 is glossed 相聽也 with 二人, while 從 is 隨從也 and analyzed as 从 plus 辵, with 从 also serving as phonetic. The editor notes that the meanings are related by extension and that oracle-bone material uses only 从; in this account, the split into two 說文 entries reflects later usage. This is an editorial historical interpretation, distinct from simply repeating Xu Shen’s Han-dynasty analysis.
evidence.title: [A01293-015] (從) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 許慎, 說文解字 (as quoted by CUHK database and Taiwan MOE dictionary)
evidence.field: 说文 entries 从部 / 辵部
evidence.text: The Han dictionary’s separate explanations are quoted as ‘从，相聽也。从二人。凡从之屬皆从从。’ and ‘從，隨行也。从辵、从，从亦聲。’ These are Xu Shen’s historical analyses, not direct proof that every component interpretation matches the earlier inscriptions. The evidence supports辵 as the movement/semantic element in the 從 analysis and 从 as its phonetic element, but the attested development still allows a semantic relation to the earlier ‘follow’ graph.
evidence.title: [A01293-015] (從) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese 從 entry (consulted as a secondary compilation; reconstruction citations identify Zhengzhang and Baxter–Sagart systems)
evidence.field: Glyph origin, pronunciation, definitions, historical phonology
evidence.text: The entry calls 從 originally written 从 and analyzes later 從 as semantic 辵 ‘walk’ plus phonetic 从. It lists Mandarin cóng and Cantonese cung4, Baxter–Sagart system 1.1 (2014) Middle Chinese ‹dzjowng› and Old Chinese /*[dz]oŋ/ for the ‘follow’ reading, and Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese /*zloŋ/ for 從 and 从. A phonetic relationship is plausible within each cited system, but the two reconstructions must not be treated as interchangeable or as establishing the exact original pronunciation of the graph. The entry also gives separate readings/senses and traditional graphs; its graph-loan discussion needs independent corroboration.
evidence.title: 從 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry describes the duplicated 人 form as an ideogrammic compound depicting one person moving with another and says modern simplified 从 is also a traditional variant form of 從. It separately notes a 1955 draft simplified use of 从 for 叢. This confirms that the modern character can have distinct writing histories by lexeme; it does not make every use a borrowing or show that simplified 从 descended graphically from the later 從 shape.
evidence.title: 从 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese 從 entry (secondary compilation citing Zhengzhang, 2003)
evidence.text: For 從, the entry lists Mandarin cóng and Cantonese cung4, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese /*zloŋ/; for the phonetic element 从 it lists Zhengzhang Old Chinese /*zloŋ/. It also lists forms such as 縱 with /*ʔsloŋ/ and /*ʔsloŋs/ in that same reconstruction system, alongside related phonetic-series members. These comparisons support a possible sound-component function for 从 in 從; they do not establish every sense’s chronology or prove the phonetic series is a complete account of formation.
evidence.title: 從 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Taiwan Ministry of Education
evidence.field: 異體字 / source record for 从-shaped variants
evidence.text: The entry explicitly cautions that 《說文》 distinguishes 从 and 從, assigning 相聽 ‘heed/obey’ to the former and 隨從 ‘follow/accompany’ to the latter, while the dictionary editor sees a semantic extension and says oracle-bone texts use only 从. This supports recording the Shuowen distinction as a historical source claim and the merger/extension as a later editorial analysis, not as an uncontested fact.

evidence.text: The editor reports that 說文 separates 从, glossed 相聽 and analyzed as 二人, from 從, glossed 隨從 and analyzed as 从 plus 辵, with 从 also described as phonetic. gaps: No graph-loan source-word claim was established for 从/從 in the inspected primary or official dictionary material; Wiktionary’s proposed Tibetan comparisons remain tentative and were not independently verified. No object-name borrowing hypothesis applies to the supported 人 + 人 graph analysis.

The exact earliest dated attestation of the graph and of each separate sense was not fixed. The sources list Shang oracle-bone catalogue identifiers and later bronze inscription identifiers but do not provide a secure absolute date for each cited example or establish a full semantic chronology.
The Academia Sinica and Zdic pages link to inscription images, but those glyph images were not visually inspected. The identified forms and readings are reported from catalogue text only.
